pw_slow_hash.note: requirements.txt pins Flask>=3.0, which pulls in Werkzeug 3.x. Its generate_password_hash defaults to salted scrypt. The method isn't set explicitly, so this relies on the library default.

token_csprng.note: Only the SHA-256 of the token is stored in the sessions table (app.py:203).

no_hardcoded_secret.note: No signing key or SECRET_KEY exists, because tokens are random rather than signed. The only literal is DUMMY_HASH = generate_password_hash("not-a-real-password") at app.py:23. It is used only to keep login timing the same, not as a secret.

token_expiry.evidence: app.py:111 if not row or row["expires_at"] < time.time():
token_expiry.note: TOKEN_TTL = 30 * 24 * 3600 (app.py:14), set at app.py:203 as now + TOKEN_TTL.

logout_revokes.evidence: app.py:213 db().execute("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE token_hash = ?", (sha(token),))
logout_revokes.note: POST /api/logout deletes the session row on the server.

owner_checks.evidence: app.py:137 "SELECT * FROM notes WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?"; app.py:263 "UPDATE ... WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?"; app.py:274 "DELETE FROM notes WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?"; app.py:285 row = get_own_note(note_id)
owner_checks.note: Read, update, delete, share and unshare are all limited to user_id = g.user_id.

share_token_strong.note: 24 random bytes = 192 bits from the secrets module.

login_rate_limit.evidence: app.py:190 if throttled(key): return err("Too many failed attempts. Try again later.", 429)
login_rate_limit.note: Allows 10 failures per (IP, email) in 600 seconds (app.py:143). The counter is kept in memory per process.

sql_parameterized.note: Every query that takes user input uses ? placeholders. No query is built with string formatting.

xss_safe_render.note: el() inserts child strings with e.append(c) (index.html:32), which creates text nodes. The shared view does the same (index.html:134). innerHTML is never used.

security_headers.note: Set in an after_request hook on all responses. The CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' for scripts.
